sourceBasis: Pediatric Dosage Simplified (Hinglish/English) — pediatric dosing and antibiotic stewardship sections
Doctorwalah OPD Gold Edition — case-specific investigation and follow-up notes

rules: Require weight before automatic pediatric dose calculation.
Do not derive a fixed-dose-combination pediatric dose from a paracetamol-only mg/kg reference.
Avoid aspirin as a routine antipyretic in children with viral fever.
Do not automatically substitute adult prescription products for pediatric patients.
Pregnancy pathway should take priority when pregnancy is documented.
Non-pregnancy pathways must not auto-select NSAIDs or fluoroquinolones in pregnancy without a pregnancy-specific reference match.
Confirm gestational age, CBC/antenatal status and medicine-specific safety before automatic selection.
Prefer the narrowest appropriate spectrum and escalate only when needed.
Use the shortest effective duration supported by the selected protocol.
Review culture/susceptibility results and de-escalate when appropriate.

Dengue Fever: Daily platelet count / warning-sign monitoring when clinically indicated
Typhoid Fever: Widal test after 1 week (as stated in source)
Acute Uncomplicated UTI: Urine culture for recurrent cases / males
Headache (Recurrent): Neuroimaging only when clinically indicated / red flags
Diabetes Mellitus (Type 2): Glucose assessment and diabetes follow-up investigations as clinically indicated
High Blood Pressure (Newly Detected): Repeat BP confirmation and appropriate cardiovascular/renal assessment as clinically indicated

followUp.Dengue Fever: 7 days / earlier immediately if warning signs; source also advises monitoring during the illness
followUp.Typhoid Fever: 3–5 days; source says reassess/change antibiotic if no response
followUp.default: Use the clinician-entered follow-up date; if absent, do not invent a date.
